recovery.guides.mini.title: reComputer Mini — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.mini.steps.1: Connect a USB Micro-B cable from the USB2.0 DEVICE port to your Ubuntu host.
recovery.guides.mini.steps.2: Use a pin to press and hold the RECOVERY button inside the hole.
recovery.guides.robotics.title: reComputer Robotics — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.robotics.steps.1: Set the DIP switch to the RESET position.
recovery.guides.robotics.steps.2: Connect the power cable and power on the carrier board.
recovery.guides.robotics.steps.3: Connect the carrier board to your Ubuntu host with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.robotics.steps.4: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.super.title: reComputer Super — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.super.steps.1: Set the DIP switch to the RESET position.
recovery.guides.super.steps.2: Connect the power cable and power on the carrier board.
recovery.guides.super.steps.3: Connect the carrier board to your Ubuntu host with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.super.steps.4: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.classic.title: reComputer J401 — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.classic.steps.1: Short the FC REC pin to GND with a jumper (see the pin diagram below).
recovery.guides.classic.steps.2: Connect the power adapter and power on the reComputer.
recovery.guides.classic.steps.3: Connect the carrier board to your Ubuntu host with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.classic.steps.4: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.classic.note: Warning: When using Orin NX 16GB/8GB modules, do not enable MAXN SUPER mode. The carrier board cooling is insufficient for that mode and may damage the module.
recovery.guides.industrial.title: reComputer Industrial — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.industrial.steps.1: Connect the USB2.0 DEVICE port to your computer with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.industrial.steps.2: Use a pin to press and hold the RECOVERY button inside the hole.
recovery.guides.industrial.steps.3: Connect the included 2-pin power connector to the board and power on.
recovery.guides.industrial.steps.5: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.reserver.title: reServer Industrial — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.reserver.steps.1: Connect the DEVICE port to your computer with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.reserver.steps.2: Use a pin to press and hold the REC button inside the hole.
recovery.guides.reserver.steps.3: Connect the included 2-pin power connector to the board and power on.
recovery.guides.reserver.steps.5: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.j501-carrier.title: reServer J501 Carrier Board — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.j501-carrier.steps.1: Connect the carrier board to your Ubuntu host with a USB Type-C cable first.
recovery.guides.j501-carrier.steps.2: Then connect the power cable and power on the board.
recovery.guides.j501-carrier.steps.5: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
recovery.guides.j501mini.title: reComputer Robotics J501 Mini — Enter Recovery Mode
recovery.guides.j501mini.steps.1: Press and hold the RESET button.
recovery.guides.j501mini.steps.2: Connect the power cable and power on the board, then release the REC button.
recovery.guides.j501mini.steps.3: Connect the carrier board to your Ubuntu host with a USB Type-C cable.
recovery.guides.j501mini.steps.4: Run lsusb on the host to confirm the device is in Recovery mode.
